environment: Python 3.14.7, node test runner, branch sdlc/S-007 in a scratch worktree, python3 -I

cases.title: parse equals a spec reference model on random formats, branches and ledgers
cases.given: Formats from 5 prefixes, 4 suffixes and both placeholders; tails built from the 8 rows, their case variants, newlines, NUL, non-ASCII digits and junk; ids as list, tuple, iterator or absent.
cases.when: parse runs 5000 times per seed for seeds 20261010, 7 and 99, and a model written from the section 2 table runs on the same input.
cases.then: Both give the same result, or both give None.
cases.actual: 0 differences in 15000 runs; every kind and null occurred (null 2678, verify 409, attempt 355, e2e 338, milestone 377, run 305, e2e-area 291, slice 202, state 45 for seed 20261010)

evidence.title: reference-model property
evidence.inline: property=parse equals model; seeds=20261010,7,99; runs=5000 each; result=pass; shrunk counterexample=none (no shrinking)

cases.title: A non-string branch, NUL, a lone surrogate, an empty or short branch and a prefix and suffix overlap give None and do not raise
cases.given: Branch values None, 5, 5.5, bytes, list, dict, True, a class, NUL in the tail and in the prefix, a lone surrogate, '', 'sdl', 'sdlc/', and format ab{name}ba with aba and abba.

cases.title: A trailing newline follows the spec regex text
cases.given: sdlc/run-2, sdlc/S-001, sdlc/M-1 and sdlc/S-001-v0-cli-0, each with one final newline; a final newline after a literal suffix; two final newlines.
cases.when: parse runs under the default format and under sdlc/{name}-wip.
cases.then: The row regex uses re.search and $, which matches before a final newline. The spec gives the regex text, so the branch classifies and tail keeps the newline. A newline after the suffix gives None. Two newlines give None.
cases.actual: run n=2, slice S-001, milestone M-1 and verify classified with tail ending in a newline; newline after suffix None; double newline None

cases.title: Non-ASCII digits match the digit groups, with no ASCII flag
cases.given: sdlc/run-<ARABIC-INDIC 3>, sdlc/run-<FULLWIDTH 2>, a verify tail with Arabic-Indic round and part, a state tail with 14 Arabic-Indic digits.
cases.then: The regexes use \d without re.ASCII, as the spec text gives, so each classifies; int() converts n, round and part.
cases.expected: classified as the spec regex text
cases.actual: run n=3, run n=2, verify round 0 part 1, state ts kept as text

cases.title: Unicode case folding under {name:lower} does not raise
cases.given: Kelvin sign, long s (U+017F), dotted capital I in the prefix and in the branch, sharp capital S, upper-case prefix.
cases.actual: no exception; U+017F matches S under re.IGNORECASE, so sdlc/<U+017F>-001 is a slice (spec says IGNORECASE; seed)

cases.title: Long tails of 40000 characters finish in bounded time
cases.given: 14 tails of 40000 characters aimed at rows 4 to 8.
cases.when: parse runs and the time is recorded.
cases.then: Each call ends in under 5 seconds. The spec states no limit.
cases.actual: slowest 1979 ms (quadratic growth on row 6: 2000 chars 2.9 ms, 4000 chars 11.4 ms, 8000 chars 45.5 ms)

evidence.title: row 6 backtracking
evidence.inline:
tail a-v1- repeated, then '!':
2000 chars 2.9 ms
4000 chars 11.4 ms
8000 chars 54.9 ms
40000 chars about 1100 ms (lower: 1979 ms)

seeds.title: parse raises ValueError for a run number of more than 4300 digits
seeds.detail: sdlc/run-<5000 digits> matches row 1; int() then raises ValueError (Python digit limit). The parse command would end with a traceback. The spec states no limit on n. A loop branch never holds such a number.

seeds.title: parse raises AttributeError for non-string ledger ids under {name:lower}
seeds.detail: ids=[5,'S-001'] or [None] under a lower format raises AttributeError on candidate.lower(). Under a plain format a non-string compares unequal and does not raise. A bare string as ids iterates characters and gives known false. ids=5 raises TypeError. The spec says ids holds ledger ids, so these inputs are out of contract.

seeds.title: row 6 regex backtracks quadratically on long tails
seeds.detail: A tail of the form a-v1-a-v1-... followed by '!' costs about 45 ms at 8000 characters and about 1.1 s at 40000. A git branch name is far shorter in practice. No limit in the spec.

seeds.title: non-ASCII digits and a trailing newline classify
seeds.detail: sdlc/run-<ARABIC-INDIC 3> gives run n=3. sdlc/run-2<LF> gives run n=2 with tail run-2<LF>. Both follow the spec regex text (no re.ASCII, re.search with $), but a stricter reader may want them rejected. A decision for the spec owner.

seeds.title: U+017F and the Kelvin sign fold under re.IGNORECASE
seeds.detail: Under {name:lower}, sdlc/<U+017F>-001 classifies as slice with id <U+017F>-001, since IGNORECASE matches U+017F to s. The prefix and suffix compare uses str.lower(), which folds differently from the regex. Follows the spec text.
